headline: The dollar squeeze narrowed to the peso while the tightening moved back into real yields — and the index made a new high on a tape where only software, cyber and metals worked.
summary: The composition of the tightening changed again. Nominal yields ground higher (2y +5bp to 4.80%, 5y +3bp to 5.02%, 10y +2bp to 5.24%, 3m bill 4.25% at the 95th percentile), but breakevens went the other way — 5y -3bp to 2.34%, 10y -2bp to 2.33%, inflation composite -25. That means the entire move is real: the 10y TIPS yield is 2.91%, +45bp on the month, z=1.74 with acceleration z=1.23, the 97th percentile of the year. Yesterday the marginal tightening was coming through FX; today the curve took it back, and it is the growth-hostile kind. Rates composite -74. The 30-year mortgage still prints 7.40%, +69bp in a month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, the 100th percentile — and housing is paying immediately, with XHB -1.0% and ITB -1.3% on a day the S&P rose 0.6%, XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.

The dollar story also narrowed. DXY is 102.23, +0.1%, still the 99.9th percentile with z=1.76 and acceleration 1.73, but EURUSD was flat, AUDUSD +0.3%, USDBRL -0.5%, USDCNY -0.3% at its 52-week low. The violence has concentrated in one currency: USDMXN +2.1% on the day to 18.36, +8.6% on the month, z=3.21 with acceleration z=2.42 — the single most extreme print in the entire digest, and it happened on firm US data. Mexican equities have not discounted a peso move of that size (MXX +1.6%, EWW +0.6% today, only -5.9% on the month). Brazil remains the mirror image: EWZ +2.2% today, +14.0% on the week, +14.4% on the month at the 100th percentile, BVSP z=2.16, with BRL the only EM currency gaining against a record dollar. LatAm is no longer one trade.

Index versus internals remains the real fracture, and it widened. SPX 7,811 (+0.6%, 99.5th percentile), NDX +0.5%, DJI +0.8%, QUAL at the 100th percentile — yet RSP/SPY sits at the 10th percentile and IWM/SPY at the 13.7th with z=-1.65. Leadership is a handful of self-funding software names: CIBR +3.6% today, +16.4% on the month, z=2.11 with acceleration 2.29 at the 100th percentile; IGV +2.8% and +10.6% on the month; PLTR +5.2% (+23.3% month, 100th percentile); MSFT +2.4%; AMZN +3.3%. Silicon is being sold to pay for it — SMH -0.6% today and -4.3% on the week, SOXX -5.0%, AMD -2.0%, MU -4.3% on the week, TSM -4.1%, KOSPI -5.0% and EWY -7.6% — with software/semis +3.5% in a day and +8.6% in a week. The new entrant is healthcare: XLV +1.6%, IBB and XBI both +3.0%, UNH +2.3%, relative strength turning up. Financials refuse to join: KRE -0.8% and KBE -0.7% red into a green tape, KRE/SPY at the 13.8th percentile, GS -13.0% on the month at z=-1.88, IAI -6.6%, BX -11.5%.

Commodities gave the cyclical bulls a second day of ammunition and the consumer a third. Copper +2.9% to 6.711 (95th percentile, 9.1% above its 200-day), copper/gold +1.4% at the 98.6th percentile, and the washed-out miners finally bid: COPX +4.3%, GDXJ +3.2%, GDX +3.0%, FCX +3.6%, XME +1.7% — all still down 10-13% on the month, so this is reflex, not trend. Precious metals bounced hard off a brutal month (gold +1.5% but -5.4% on the month; silver +3.5% after -10.1%; platinum +4.3% after -11.4%). Energy is splitting: Brent 104.43 (+2.1% on the week, +3.2% month) against WTI -4.6% on the month, while RBOB fell another 5.4% today — crude is a spread story, gasoline is pure consumer relief. Hedging stays absurdly cheap and suspiciously bid at the same time: VIX 14.84 (-3.7%, 8th percentile), VIX3M 17.77 (3rd percentile), but SKEW +3.5% to 154.34 at the 79th percentile. Credit composite +48 with HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile — but HYG itself is rolling over at z=-1.18 and LQD -2.3% on the month at the 10th percentile. That is duration leaking into spread product, not a credit event. Own the self-funders and the metals; short anything that requires cheaper money.

good.text: New index highs with participation at the top: S&P 7,811 (+0.6%, 99.5th percentile), Dow +0.8%, Nasdaq 100 +0.5%, QUAL at the 100th percentile and high-beta/low-vol +1.2% on the day, +6.6% on the month.

Cyber and software are accelerating, not just rising: CIBR +3.6% today, +16.4% on the month, z=2.11 with acceleration z=2.29 at the 100th percentile; IGV +2.8% and +10.6%; PLTR +5.2%; MSFT +2.4% with acceleration 1.04.

The growth-metal signal survived the month-long washout: copper +2.9% at the 95th percentile and 9.1% above its 200-day, copper/gold +1.4% at the 98.6th percentile, with COPX +4.3% and FCX +3.6% turning up off deeply negative z-scores.

Inflation expectations are deflating while the consumer gets pump relief: 5y breakeven -3bp to 2.34% at the 32nd percentile, 10y -2bp, RBOB -5.4% on the day and -2.3% on the month, corn -3.9%, wheat -1.8%.
Brazil keeps compounding against a record dollar: EWZ +2.2% today, +14.0% on the week, 100th percentile; BVSP z=2.16; USDBRL -0.5% today and -4.4% on the week.
Healthcare is a genuinely new leadership leg: XLV +1.6% with relative strength turning up, IBB +3.0%, XBI +3.0%, UNH +2.3%, LLY acceleration z=1.03.

bad.text: The tightening is now purely real and still speeding up: 10y TIPS yield 2.91%, +45bp on the month, z=1.74 with acceleration 1.23, 97th percentile, against falling breakevens. Rates composite -74.

Mortgages at 7.40% (+69bp in a month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, 100th percentile) are killing housing in real time — XHB -1.0% and ITB -1.3% on a +0.6% S&P day, XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.
Breadth never healed: RSP/SPY at the 10th percentile, IWM/SPY at the 13.7th with z=-1.65, Dow Transports rolling over, breadth composite -14 on a day every index closed green.

The peso is in a disorderly move — USDMXN +2.1% on the day, +8.6% on the month, z=3.21 with acceleration z=2.42, the most extreme print in the digest — and Mexican equities (MXX +1.6%, EWW +0.6%) have not discounted any of it.
Financials are the persistent leak: KRE -0.8% and KBE -0.7% into a rally, KRE/SPY at the 13.8th percentile, GS -13.0% on the month at z=-1.88, IAI -6.6%, BX -11.5%, XLF -6.0% relative.

Anything needing cheap capital or power is still being liquidated: NLR -15.9% on the month (z=-2.25, 1.6th percentile), REMX -20.1% (0.8th), URA -17.0%, TAN -8.4% at the 2nd percentile, ORCL -12.5%. Deere -4.8% in a day, -9.6% in a week, says the capex cycle is cracking too.

trades.name: Long software/cyber vs short semis
trades.line: Long IGV+CIBR vs short SMH: code is eating silicon's bid
trades.expr: Long equal notional IGV and CIBR versus short SMH, dollar-neutral, rebalanced weekly. Cash equity or swap.
trades.thesis: With real yields at 2.91% and rising, capital is rotating from capex-heavy, cyclically-priced silicon into cash-generative software and security spend that does not need a weaker dollar or cheaper debt. CIBR's acceleration z of 2.29 at the 100th percentile with z=2.11 is the strongest trending series in the digest.
trades.trigger: IGV +2.8% and CIBR +3.6% today while SMH -0.6% and -4.3% on the week; software/semis ratio +3.5% in a day, +8.6% in a week, +23.5% over three months. TSM -4.1%, MU -4.3%, AMD -4.1% on the week with Korea -5.0%.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH closing back below its level of a week ago (a 8%+ give-back), or CIBR acceleration z turning negative with the ETF losing its 50-day.
trades.target: Another 8-10% on the ratio over the next quarter; IGV toward +20% on the month-over-month trend, SMH relative back to flat YTD-adjusted.

trades.name: Short homebuilders
trades.line: Short XHB/ITB into a 7.40% mortgage at a 52-wk extreme
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy 3-month ITB put spreads ~10% out of the money; alternatively short XHB vs long SPY to isolate the rate transmission.
trades.thesis: The 30-year mortgage at 7.40% is +69bp in a month with acceleration z=1.5 and sits at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks. Shelter demand is being destroyed at the margin and the equities are only now rolling, with XHB/SPY already at the 0th percentile — relative lows usually lead absolute lows.
trades.trigger: ITB -1.3% and XHB -1.0% on a day the S&P rose 0.6%; ITB -12.6% over three months and in the 0.2 percentile of its 52-week range; DHI -0.7%, HD -1.6%; 10y real yield +4bp with breakevens falling.
trades.stop: 10y real yield back under 2.60% or mortgage rate printing below 7.00%, or XHB/SPY making a 1-month relative high.
trades.target: ITB down another 10-12% toward the lower end of its three-month range; XHB/SPY -6%.

trades.name: Long Brazil vs short Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ vs short EWW: BRL compounding, MXN cracking
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal dollar notional. Add a long USDMXN 3-month call spread (18.50/19.50 strikes) as the convex leg.
trades.thesis: LatAm has split into two regimes. Brazil has a strengthening currency, equities at a 52-week high and an accelerating trend; Mexico has a currency in a three-standard-deviation break while its equity index trades like nothing is happening. Equity markets lag currency breaks of this magnitude.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +2.1% today, +8.6% on the month, z=3.21 with acceleration z=2.42; USDBRL -0.5% today and -4.4% on the week; EWZ +2.2% today, +14.0% on the week at the 100th percentile; EWW only -5.9% on the month and MXX actually +1.6% today.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.60 (unwinding the month's move) or EWZ losing 10% from entry while EWW outperforms two weeks running.

trades.name: Copper miners catch-up
trades.line: Long COPX/FCX: copper at 95th pctile, miners -10% on month
trades.expr: Long COPX, with FCX as the single-name expression for size; fund by shorting XME if you want the pure copper-versus-diversified-mining spread.
trades.thesis: Copper is the cleanest growth signal left and it is holding near highs while the equities were liquidated with the rest of the resource complex. Copper/gold at the 98.6th percentile says the cycle is not rolling over; the miners are mispriced to the metal.
trades.trigger: Copper +2.9% to 6.711 (95th percentile, 9.1% above its 200-day) and +3.4% on the week; COPX +4.3% and turning up from z=-1.23 after -10.0% on the month; FCX +3.6%; copper/gold +1.4% on the day, +4.3% on the month.
trades.stop: Copper closing below 6.30 or copper/gold rolling over below its 200-day; COPX failing to reclaim its 50-day within three weeks.
trades.target: COPX +15% to recover the month's drawdown; FCX toward 85.

trades.name: Cheap convexity on the index
trades.line: Buy SPX downside: VIX 8th pctile, SKEW 79th, breadth 10th
trades.expr: Buy 3-month SPX put spreads ~5% / 12% out of the money, or 1x2 VIX call spreads (Dec 18/25). Funded partly by selling short-dated upside in IWM.
trades.thesis: You are being handed the cheapest insurance of the year into the narrowest tape of the year. The index is at a 99.5th-percentile high while equal-weight and small-cap relatives sit at the 10th and 14th percentiles — that combination only resolves by breadth catching up or the mega-caps giving back. Someone is already paying for the tails.
trades.trigger: VIX 14.84 (-3.7%, 8th percentile), VIX3M 17.77 (3rd percentile), term structure 0.835 — yet SKEW +3.5% to 154.34 at the 79th percentile; RSP/SPY -2.7% on the month, IWM/SPY -6.0% with z=-1.65; MOVE still +28.3% on the month at z=1.5.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY both reclaiming their 1-month highs (breadth resolving upward), or VIX3M below 16 with SKEW falling back under 145.
trades.target: 2-3x on the put spread on a 5-7% index drawdown; VIX 22+.

trades.name: Long healthcare vs short banks
trades.line: Long XLV vs short KBE: new leadership vs the persistent leak
trades.expr: Long XLV (add IBB for beta) versus short KBE or KRE, equal notional.
trades.thesis: Healthcare is the only new sector leadership in the tape, broad across large biotech, small biotech and managed care. Banks are the one group that cannot catch a bid even on green days: the 2-year at 4.80% (+37bp on the month) raises funding costs while 2s10s flattened 3bp today, and the capital-markets complex is in outright drawdown.
trades.trigger: XLV +1.6% with relative strength turning up and IBB/XBI both +3.0%, against KBE -0.7% and KRE -0.8% on a +0.6% S&P day; KRE/SPY at the 13.8th percentile with z=-1.04; GS -13.0% on the month at z=-1.88, IAI -6.6%, BX -11.5%.
trades.stop: 2s10s steepening more than 25bp from here with KRE/SPY making a 1-month high, or XLV relative strength rolling back over.

trades.name: Short the capex periphery
trades.line: Short DE and PAVE: the machinery cycle is cracking
trades.expr: Short DE outright or via 3-month puts; pair with a short in PAVE against long SPY if you want sector-neutrality.
trades.thesis: Falling crop prices plus 7%+ financing costs plus a record dollar is the worst possible mix for farm and heavy equipment. Industrials relative strength is already in a downtrend and the infrastructure/capex basket is quietly failing while the index makes highs.
trades.trigger: DE -4.8% today and -9.6% on the week with z=-1.27 and acceleration z=-1.66; corn -3.9%, wheat -1.8%, soybeans flat; CAT -5.3% on the week and -15.8% over three months; PAVE -5.7% on three months with XLI relative -9.8%.
trades.stop: DE recovering the week's loss and corn turning up through its 1-month high; or XLI relative strength turning up.
